title: Choose Veny's visual world
question: The roll assigned Bombay Deco Nights. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll. Sketches show the customer home, first screen.

options.label: Bombay Deco Nights
options.lineage: Marine Drive and Eros-cinema Art Deco, Mumbai 1930s
options.thesis: The Elite Marketplace dressed like the city's grandest Deco foyer at night: geometric, gilded, calm.
options.viewport: Dark ink header with location and search; a high-contrast Didone headline; categories as stepped Deco tiles; verified pros shown with their next free slot.
options.risk: If the stepped frames multiply, it tips into theme-park Deco; they must stay limited to the verification seal and the slot picker.

raised.raise: Importance is carried by one fixed ramp (size and weight), never by extra colours.
Panels divide with brass hairline seams instead of shadows; destructive actions such as cancel or reject stand apart behind empty space.
On a phone, the service photo owns the whole first screen of service detail, with Book anchored low.
A vendor's day reads as time-ranked rows whose status restyles the row in place, never jumping position.

options.label: The Assay Certificate
options.lineage: BIS hallmark and assay certificates for gold
options.thesis: Every pro arrives hallmarked: verification shown as a certificate, with a serial, a date and a seal.
options.viewport: Search-first home; each pro card carries an assay strip (verified on, service area, next slot) and a violet seal.
options.risk: The most direct expression of 'verified', and so the most familiar; trust-badge patterns are common in this category.

options.label: Boarding Pass
options.lineage: airline boarding passes and gate boards
options.thesis: Every booking is a pass: segmented, numbered, and tracked on a live board.
options.viewport: Home leads with your next booking as a pass (pro, date, slot, booking no.); below it, available pros ranked by next free time.
options.case: Fuses cleanly: bookings map to passes and the vendor inbox to a gate board. It wins on clarity but loses on the 'elite' identity.
options.risk: Reads like travel software if the purple and type are timid.

options.label: Metro Line
options.lineage: Delhi and Namma Metro line diagrams (the Violet Line)
options.thesis: Each booking rides a line: requested, confirmed, on the way, done, drawn as stations on the violet route.
options.viewport: Midnight enamel header; the six categories as coloured lines; your active booking drawn as a station diagram.
options.case: Strong product clarity for booking status, and metro riders know it by heart; less premium than Deco.
options.risk: Many line colours can fight the single purple brand accent.

options.label: Dark Console
options.thesis: Graphite panels with hairline seams and isolated destructive actions.
options.case: Households don't identify with a developer tool.
options.kept: Hairline seams and isolated destructive actions.

options.label: Star Atlas
options.thesis: Importance as dot magnitude on a navy chart.
options.viewport: A chart of pros as stars.
options.case: Revives the rejected cosmic theme of the old app.

options.label: Vertical Feed
options.thesis: One service fills the screen and the next is one flick away.
options.case: Comparing pros needs a list, not a feed.
options.kept: The photo owns the first screen of mobile service detail.

options.label: Split-Flap Board
options.thesis: Bookings as rows on a rush-hour board.
options.case: Too mechanical for a home-services brand.
options.kept: Time-ranked rows that restyle in place.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What home-services apps ship (a clean grid, rounded cards, photo tiles), executed impeccably in dark mode with a violet accent.
canonCard.viewport: Search bar hero, category icon row, popular-services cards.
canonCard.risk: Looks like Urban Company in dark mode, with no distinct identity.
